title: OpenTable weekly seated-diner growth, New York (manual capture)
brief: Revision 2: parked, draft (owner decision, 2026-11-08). The only action is the drafted question to OpenTable (see Source). No capture of any kind is made: not automated and not manual. The work stays parked until OpenTable gives written permission and a maintainer clears it. Why: OpenTable's Terms of Use limit the content to 'personal use' and bar any 'automatic or manual device, process, or means to access, copy, search, or monitor' it 'except as expressly authorized by OpenTable'. The site also did not respond to an honest fetch from here, so nothing was measured. The rules below are rev 1's manual-capture design, kept only as the starting point if permission arrives. They are not in effect.
question: What year-over-year percentage change in seated diners from online reservations will OpenTable's State of the Industry dashboard show for New York for the target dashboard week, as displayed (rounded down by OpenTable) in the first SSA capture at or after the resolution time?

source.publisher: OpenTable, Inc. (part of Booking Holdings), 425 Market Street, San Francisco. State of the Industry dashboard. Contact on the page: commsteam@opentable.com [verified from the Wayback copy of 2026-10-26].
source.access: PARKED (rev 2): no capture of any kind, automated or manual, until written permission arrives and a maintainer clears it. The design that follows is rev 1's, kept for reference only. Manual capture only, the YouGov crosstab pattern (docs/sources/yougov.md; tools/pull_yougov_xtab.py and tools/ingest_yougov_xtab.py on origin/dev), and only once written permission exists. Who: one named SSA maintainer, the same person who does the weekly YouGov pull, with a named backup. When: once a week, on the day after each dashboard week ends, at 12:00 America/New_York. That one capture is both the resolution capture for the week that ended two weeks before and the lock-time reference capture for the next round (see lock). What: in an ordinary browser, open the dashboard, choose the 'Change in seated diners by month / week / day' table, the weekly view and the New York label. Record a full-page screenshot plus a typed JSON line: {geo, view:'week', week_end, value_pct, captured_at_utc, methodology_note}. Ingest: a new tools/ingest_opentable_soti.py modelled on ingest_yougov_xtab.py. It checks that week_end equals the expected week, that value_pct is an integer, that geo matches the frozen label, and that the methodology text still says 'online reservations only'. It refuses a capture day older than the newest archive. It writes sources/opentable_soti/<capture-day>.png and .json with sha256 values in sources/manifest.json. Missed capture: if none lands within 48 hours of the scheduled time, the rounds that depend on it are void (resolution) or not posted (lock). Never back-fill later. No fetcher, scraper or headless browser. The page loads its numbers from https://www.opentable.com/c/wapi/r9-ot-soti/v1/data. That endpoint is named here only so the permission question can be specific, and it is not used. Access test from here: an honest-user-agent curl of /legal/terms-and-conditions and of the dashboard got no response at all for more than 4 minutes (2026-11-09T01:03Z). WebFetch of /c/legal/terms-and-conditions/ timed out at 60 s twice. Treat that as bot protection, and as an access risk even for a courier (lesson 3).
source.archive_policy: Use: unclear. Automated retrieval: barred. Manual capture and archiving: barred unless OpenTable authorizes it. Redistribution: barred unless OpenTable authorizes it. Evidence, all from the Terms of Use as archived by the Wayback Machine on 2026-10-28 (the live page did not respond). §11 'Intellectual Property Rights and Grant of Rights to User': all 'text, graphical content, video, data, and other content made available through the Services (collectively, the "OpenTable Content")' are provided 'solely to support User's permitted use of the Services ... no license is granted to User for any other purpose'. §13 'Use Restrictions': 'The Services and OpenTable Content are offered solely for User's personal use for the purposes described in this Agreement. Any and all other uses are prohibited.' In the same section, users agree not to '(1) use any deep-link, robot, spider, scraper, generative AI or other AI technology ... or other automatic or manual device, process, or means to access, copy, search, or monitor any portion of the Services or OpenTable Content, except as expressly authorized by OpenTable' [verified text]. The dashboard page itself says twice: 'If using data from the dashboard, please cite OpenTable and link back to this site' [verified, Wayback copy of 2026-10-26]. Reading: the page invites citation, which suggests OpenTable expects others to use the figures. It does not expressly authorize archiving copies, weekly monitoring or redistribution, and §13 names 'manual' means. The manual YouGov route does not get around this, because these terms bar the manual route too. Proposed inventory row: 'permission-needed', proposed for maintainers and not granted. The agent does not decide it. Task for a person, once a maintainer says go (nobody sends anything before that): send the following message to commsteam@opentable.com, from an SSA address, and record the reply and its date in this card's evidence. Message: 'We run a non-commercial public research benchmark that asks models to forecast published indicators before they appear. We would like to use the State of the Industry dashboard's weekly year-over-year seated-diner figure for New York. Once a week, a person would view the dashboard and record the displayed value with a screenshot, and we would publish that value with a citation and link to the dashboard. Do you authorize this use under section 13 of the Terms of Use? May we keep and publish the screenshots? Could we instead read the dashboard's data endpoint (r9-ot-soti/v1/data) once a week?'

target.population: Seated diners from online reservations at restaurants active on OpenTable in the dashboard's 'New York' geography during the week (the dashboard's methodology). Only geographies with 50 or more platform restaurants are shown. The label is where people dine, not where diners live. Platform coverage changes, so the series mixes behaviour with coverage (the doc).
target.window: One dashboard week as OpenTable defines it. The methodology's example, 'the week ending on January 6, 2026', is a Tuesday, so weeks may end on Tuesdays [unverified; the pilot records it]. Days are compared by weekday ('Tuesday of week 1 in 2026 to Tuesday of week 1 in 2025'), not by date.
target.calculation: The integer percentage shown in the dashboard's weekly table for New York for the target week, as captured. Use the published weekly value, never an average of daily values (the doc). OpenTable rounds the figure down.
target.unit: Percent change in seated diners against the same week of the previous year (integer, rounded down by OpenTable)

lock: 23:59 America/New_York on the last day of the dashboard week before the target week (the doc: 'Lock before the source-defined target window begins, using an explicit time zone'). The week ending at the lock has not been published at lock, so the reference uses the newest week in the lock capture, normally the week before that (lesson 9). The capture happens on the day before the lock. Earliest first scored lock: not before written permission. If permission arrived by Fri 2026-11-27 and the ingest tool reached main by about 2026-12-04, four weekly pilot captures (Dec 2026) would measure the week definition, posting lag and revisions, and the first scored lock could be about Tue 2027-01-12 [inferred, conditional].
baseline: Ranked zero point: persistence, the newest completed week's published percentage in the lock capture (the doc: 'the previous completed week's published growth as persistence'). Spread: RMS of persistence's own errors over the 13 most recent weeks in the lock capture, the yoy4 pattern from track/seattle-community-calls-v2. A fixed sd of 1.5 would be a point forecast if weekly changes run several points. Shown, not ranked: the trailing four-week mean of published weekly percentages (the doc's robustness check). Not measured. No dashboard data was read: the live site did not respond to an honest fetch, and reading the archived data endpoint would copy OpenTable Content against §13. The first job of the pilot is the backtest on the dashboard's own weekly history for the current year, once permission allows it.
resolution: The first ingested capture at or after 12:00 America/New_York on the day after the week following the target week ends, so about 8 days after the target week ends, inside a 48-hour grace window. The pilot measures how soon a completed week appears and whether it changes. If it posts the next day and never changes, a later revision can shorten the lag. Later dashboard changes never alter a resolved round.
missing_data_policy: (1) No valid capture inside the grace window: the round is void. (2) New York missing from the weekly view (below the 50-restaurant floor, or relabelled): void, and the label list is reviewed. (3) A methodology change (for example, dropping 'online reservations only'): rounds that have not resolved are void, and a new revision is needed. (4) No capture at the lock-reference time: the round is not posted. (5) Ties from rounding down count as published.
scoring: SSA topline scoring of a predictive distribution over the published percentage, scored with CRPS (continuous_normal, mean and sd or quantiles). Skill = 1 - CRPS(entrant) / CRPS(persistence with its 13-week RMS spread). The rounded-down integer target puts a floor of about 0.29 points on achievable CRPS. That is small if weekly moves are several points, and the pilot checks this with arena scoring.noise_floor before any round is scored. The doc's profile (several cities in a holiday week, energy score) and ranking (RBO with a fixed tie rule) come after the number works.

evidence.finding: [verified text, Wayback copy fetched 2026-11-09T01:09:35Z] OpenTable Terms of Use. §11: OpenTable Content, including 'data', is provided 'solely to support User's permitted use of the Services ... no license is granted to User for any other purpose'. §13 'Use Restrictions': 'offered solely for User's personal use ... Any and all other uses are prohibited'. Users may not 'use any deep-link, robot, spider, scraper, generative AI or other AI technology ... or other automatic or manual device, process, or means to access, copy, search, or monitor any portion of the Services or OpenTable Content, except as expressly authorized by OpenTable'. The Agreement contains an arbitration provision with a class-action waiver.

[verified text, Wayback copy fetched 2026-11-09T01:09:41Z] The dashboard draws on 'more than 70,000 restaurants'. It shows YoY change in 'seated diners from online reservations only' (methodology updated June 2024), compares the same weekday of the same week, covers regions or metros with 50 or more restaurants, rounds percentages down, and makes no adjustment for holidays, tourism, events or weather. There are daily, weekly and monthly views, and the current month is month-to-date. The example 'week ending on January 6, 2026' is a Tuesday. The page says twice: 'If using data from the dashboard, please cite OpenTable and link back to this site'. There is no download or export link in the HTML. The figures load from https://www.opentable.com/c/wapi/r9-ot-soti/v1/data (r9SotiData.endpoint), which was not fetched.

[verified 2026-11-09T01:03:16Z] An honest-user-agent curl got no response for more than 4 minutes and was stopped. WebFetch of https://www.opentable.com/c/legal/terms-and-conditions/ timed out at 60 s, twice, between 01:07Z and 01:08Z. The dashboard and robots.txt were queued in the same run and never reached. This is consistent with bot protection that holds non-browser clients without answering. The block was not worked around.

[verified 2026-11-09] The Wayback Machine has a capture of the data endpoint from 2026-10-10. The agent did not open it. Reading OpenTable Content from an archive would copy it by automatic means (§13), and it would also get around the live block.

[owner input] Written under 'Contact: donghang@mit.edu', but the overview's Contacts table and its list of 12 datasets do not include this section. The doc proposes a named city's next complete week, a holiday-week city profile and a city ranking; lock before the window; a pilot to measure lag and revisions; and persistence on the previous completed week plus a 4-week check. It says that the attribution request 'alone does not establish permission'. That is correct, and the terms go further than the doc says: they bar manual copying and monitoring as well.

open_questions: Maintainers: decide whether, and when, a person sends the drafted question in source.archive_policy to commsteam@opentable.com. Until a written answer authorizes it, the card stays parked and no capture of any kind is made. City choice, question type and lock day (rev 1's other open questions) wait for that answer.
assumptions: Rev 2, owner decision (Claude, delegated by Haoyang Shang, 2026-11-08): stays draft and parked. The only action is the drafted question to OpenTable, and no capture of any kind is made. Rev 1's open questions on city, question type and lock day are deferred until there is an answer. Their rev 1 recommendations were New York, one weekly number, and a lock at the end of the prior dashboard week.

Lesson 14 tests as written. Behavioral: pass (seated diners). Spatial: pass (metro labels). Recurring: likely, with views updated over time, but no schedule is published (doc), so this is unverified. Public and archivable: free to view, but the terms bar keeping a copy without authorization, so this fails as things stand. Prospective: pass (lock before the week). Scorable: pass (one published number), with rounding down.

Manual capture designed per the owner's 2026-11-08 instruction (the YouGov route), even though the terms also bar manual copying. Reason: so that a single permission answer lets implementation start. Runner-up: a blocked draft with no design.

Persistence's spread follows the Seattle yoy4 rule (13-week RMS), not the arena's fixed 1.5. Reason: lesson 12. Runner-up: the fixed 1.5 points, which may be reasonable if the weekly percentage barely moves. Unmeasured.

Suggested arena names, if it goes ahead: tracker 'opentable'; series 'opentable_nyc_weekly'; tools/ingest_opentable_soti.py; archive sources/opentable_soti/<YYYY-MM-DD>.{json,png}; round_id 'opentable-nyc-<week-end YYYY-MM-DD>'.
